findings.F1: The hourly reversal is real but far too small to trade. On every bar, the next-hour slope on the scaled 1-hour move has a t of -11.4 over 413,189 cases. Even the top decile of hourly moves gives back only +2.76 bp (t 4.0), against a trade cost of 19 bp. That is why a book trading 20.77 times a day ends at Sharpe -13.77 and -98.6 % a year.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 24-hour return relative to its 24-hour volatility, the more its return over the next 24 hours runs the opposite way, in periods when its 24-hour volatility is high against its own volatility of the past 30 days.
ideas.consequence: In a volatile stretch, a trader would lean against a coin's large daily move for about a day, more as the move is larger, and would refuse to chase it.
ideas.name: volatile-day move reversal
